explanation: In Saudi Arabia, cheek kissing between men is a common greeting among close friends or relatives, but it is strictly avoided between unrelated men and women in public due to conservative Islamic norms. Even among same-gender acquaintances, it is reserved for those with an established close relationship, not for first-time or casual social gatherings.
local_tip: When greeting a Saudi man, offer a handshake only if he extends his hand first; for a Saudi woman, wait for her to initiate any physical greeting, and never offer your hand to a woman unless she does so.
regional_note: In more cosmopolitan cities like Jeddah or Riyadh, younger Saudis may be slightly more relaxed, but the general rule of avoiding cross-gender physical contact remains widely observed.

also_check.note: Similar to Saudi Arabia, but cheek kissing among same-gender friends is more common; cross-gender greeting still requires caution.
Cheek kissing is common between same-gender friends and even between men and women in social settings, though it may be less common in conservative areas.
Cheek kissing is not a traditional greeting and can be seen as an invasion of personal space; a bow or handshake is preferred.
